title: Shot fired at Khulna NGO manager's home after he refused Tk 6.5 lakh extortion demand
excerpt: Milton Barikdar of the NGO CAS Ava Centre said three masked men came to his house. He had already complained to police on 16 November.

image.alt: A road in Khulna city with an auto-rickshaw parked by the shops
image.credit: File photo: CAPTAIN RAJU / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Three masked men fired a warning shot towards the home of an NGO manager in Khulna city on Wednesday afternoon (25 November) after he refused to pay extortion, Prothom Alo reported. The incident happened at about 2:30pm in the Dakshin Tutpara Christian Para area, next to the Chhoto Khalpar Janakalyan School. Police visited the scene.

Milton Barikdar, general manager of the NGO CAS Ava Centre, told Prothom Alo that a group had been demanding Tk 6.5 lakh from him. He said they wanted Tk 2.5 lakh to free four of their members who had been detained, and Tk 5,000 each for 70 members, a total of Tk 3.5 lakh, "for sweets".

He said three masked men arrived by motorcycle, called his wife and asked for him to come out. When she shut the gate, they abused her and fired a warning shot towards the house before leaving. Barikdar had filed a written complaint at Khulna Sadar police station on 16 November, saying he and his family were being threatened, harassed and asked for money by a local man and his associates.

Md Shafiqul Islam, assistant commissioner of Khulna Metropolitan Police (Khulna zone), told Prothom Alo that police had detained two people about 10 days ago after the complaint. They were later released on a bond into the care of Barikdar, a local church pastor and others, who said they would settle the matter themselves. After the shooting, police asked Barikdar to file a fresh case and said legal action would follow.

The incident came a day after shootings at six places in Khulna city on Tuesday, including one in which a local Awami League organising secretary was shot dead in Daulatpur, the newspaper reported. The account of the extortion demand is Barikdar's; Devlens has not been able to verify it independently.

Why it matters

Local NGO staff are visible in their communities and handle money, which can make them targets. Organisations working in Khulna and other cities with rising violence may need to review staff security, including home addresses, reporting routes and support for staff who face threats. The case also shows the risk of settling complaints informally.

What to watch

  • Whether police register a case and make arrests.
  • Any wider pattern of extortion against NGO staff in Khulna.
  • Security guidance for NGOs from the district administration or NGO networks.

Sources

  • Prothom Alo: Blank shot fired at NGO official's house in Khulna after extortion refused (Bangla), 25 November 2026
